title: Setting Up Cloud Deception with Microsoft Azure

blocks.text: This integration guide provides information on prerequisites and how to integrate Microsoft Azure with Zscaler Deception to set up Cloud Deception by deploying various Azure-specific decoy resources.
Before you set up Cloud Deception with Azure, ensure that you have:

blocks.item: A Microsoft Azure Account with a valid subscription.
An Azure user with Cloud Device Administrator and Global Administrator roles to run the deployment script.
Enabled the Restrict access to Azure AD administration portal option under User settings. This restricts decoy users from accessing the administrator portal.
Microsoft.Web and Microsoft.Insights are registered under resource providers in your subscriptions.

blocks.text: Follow these steps to set up Cloud Deception with Microsoft Azure:

blocks.item: Step 1: Configure the Integration between Azure and Deception
To integrate Microsoft Azure with Deception:
Log in to the Zscaler Deception Admin Portal.
Go to Deceive > Cloud Deception > Azure > Settings.
On the Settings page, click Add Account.
The Azure Account Setting window appears.
In the Azure Account Setting window:
Enabled: Select to enable the Azure account.
Region: Select the region of your Azure account from the drop-down menu.
Subscription ID: Enter the subscription ID of your Azure account.
Tenant ID: Enter the Azure tenant ID.

Deployment Method: Select the method you want to use to deploy resources to your Azure environment. Choose Terraform for automated Infrastructure as Code (IaC)-based deployment, or choose CloudShell for deployment through Azure's interactive shell environment.
The deployment method cannot be modified for the same configuration. If you want to change the deployment method, delete the old configuration and create a new one.
Decoy Manager Resource Group: Enter a name for the group to hold all necessary resources other than decoys to support Cloud Deception functionalities.
See image.
Click Save.
After adding the account to the Deception Admin Portal, deploy the resources in Azure cloud using one of the selected methods:
Terraform-based deployment
On the Cloud Deception - Azure page, go to Settings.
Locate the Azure account you added, and click the Download icon in the Actions column.
See image.
In the Terraform Deployment Steps window, click Download to download the necessary files.
See image.
A ZIP file containing all necessary files is downloaded to your system.
Extract the downloaded ZIP file and open the azure-decoys.tf.json file in a text editor.
Locate the backend block in the azure-decoys.tf.json file. Add your back-end details and save the file.
The following example shows a backend block of an Azure blob storage-based Terraform back end:

{ "terraform": { "backend": { "azurerm": { "resource_group_name": "your-tfstate-rg", "storage_account_name": "yourtfstatestorageacct", "container_name": "tfstate", "key": "deception/terraform.tfstate" } } } }
Ensure that you use the same back end for all configurations relating to the same Azure account.
In the terminal, go to the extracted folder, and run the following command to create a new workspace:
terraform init && terraform workspace new <workspace_name>
Run the following command to deploy resources:
terraform apply
Review the plan, and confirm it by entering Yes when prompted.
The necessary resources are deployed.
Run the following command to download the details of the state as a JSON file.
terraform output -json decoys_output > deployment-output.json
A JSON file containing the details of the state is downloaded.
On the Cloud Deception - Azure page, go to Settings, locate the Azure account you added, and click the Upload icon in the Actions column.
See image.
Select the downloaded JSON file to update the status to the Deception Admin Portal.
Cloud Shell-based deployment
On the Cloud Deception - Azure page, go to Settings.
Click Download Deployment Script.
See image.
In the Download Deployment Script window, obtain the PowerShell command using one of the following methods:
Automated Download Method

Using this method, you can obtain a PowerShell command that automatically downloads and runs the deployment script when executed via Azure's Cloud Shell. To obtain the command, copy the command from the Automated: Run the following command in Azure Cloud Shell section and save it for later use.
See image.
Manual Download Method

Using this method, you can download the deployment script as a PSM1 file, upload it to the Azure cloud, and run the script using a PowerShell command obtained from the Deception Admin Portal. To obtain the command and script:
In the Download Script Deployment window:
Click Download.
See image.
The deployment script is downloaded to your system.
Copy the command from the Manual: Download the script and run the following command in Azure Cloud Shell section, and save it for later use.
See image.
Sign in to the Azure Portal as a user with the roles mentioned in the prerequisite section.
Click the Cloud Shell icon on the top navigation bar.
See image.
In the Cloud Shell window:
Click the Upload/Download Files icon, then select Upload.
See image.
Choose the deployment script file (.psm1) that you downloaded to your system to upload it to Azure.
Sign in to the Azure Portal as a user with the roles mentioned in the prerequisites section.
Launch Cloud Shell by clicking the Cloud Shell icon on the top navigation bar.
See image.
The Cloud Shell window appears.
In the Cloud Shell window:
Set your shell environment to PowerShell.
Run the deployment script using the command obtained via the automated download method or manual download method.
Enter the option to sync settings and press Enter.
See image.

Upon successful deployment, all necessary resources are created in Azure and the information is communicated to the Deception Admin Portal. The script also installs a health function app that polls the Azure account every 15 minutes to check and update the health status of the deployed decoys. The following table lists all resources created or fetched on Azure by the deployment script:

table: A resource group created by the deployment script in Azure to hold all necessary resources other than decoys to support Cloud Deception functionalities.
A client ID assigned by Azure for decoy resources.
A secret value generated by Azure for decoy resources.
A storage account created by deployment script for logging purposes.
A function app installed by the deployment script for monitoring and updating the health status of the deployed decoys.
A role in Azure created by the deployment app to define access control for decoys.
An app service plan created for decoy app services.

blocks.item: You can set up and manage Cloud Deception for Azure separately based on the combination of Tenant ID and Subscription ID. For example, you can add multiple accounts that share the same Tenant ID but have different Subscription IDs.
Step 2: Configure the Azure Decoys
After successful integration of Azure with Deception, you can deploy various Azure-specific decoy resources. To learn how to configure the Azure decoys, see:
User Decoys
Service Principal Decoys
Managed Identity Decoys
App Service Decoys
Storage Account Container Decoys
Storage Account File Share Decoys
Key Vault Decoys
ARM Template Decoys
Container Registry Decoys
VM Image Decoys
Gen AI Decoys
Step 3: Configure Lures Using Azure Decoys

After deploying the necessary decoys based on your requirements, you can configure the lures for the decoys. To learn how to configure lures using Azure decoys, see Configuring Lures Using Azure Decoys.
